work: Pausanias' description of Greece, Volume I. + II.

items.name: the sceptre of Agamemnon
items.description: Sceptre worshipped at Chaeronea with daily sacrifices.

items.name: the statue of Zeus at Olympia
items.description: Gold and ivory statue of Zeus on an adorned throne, made by Phidias for his temple at Olympia.

wikipedia.lead: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia was a giant seated figure, about 12.4 m (41 ft) tall, made by the Greek sculptor Phidias around 435 BC at the sanctuary of Olympia, Greece, and erected in the Temple of Zeus there. Zeus is the sky and thunder god in ancient Greek religion, who rules as king of the gods on Mount Olympus.

items.name: the necklace of Harmonia
items.description: Cursed necklace for which Alcmæon was killed by Phegeus' sons.

wikipedia.lead: The Necklace of Harmonia, also called the Necklace of Eriphyle, was a fabled object in Greek mythology that, according to legend, brought great misfortune to all of its wearers or owners, who were primarily queens and princesses of the ill-fated House of Thebes.

items.name: the shield of Aristomenes
items.description: Shield Aristomenes hung in Athene's temple at Sparta, later dedicated at Lebadea.

items.name: the Argo
items.description: Jason's ship, whose mooring place Tipha claims.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts. The ship was built with divine aid and carried the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece from Iolcos to Colchis.

items.name: the Palladium
items.description: Ancient statue of Athene; Argives claim it, Pausanias doubts it.

wikipedia.lead: A palladium or palladion (plural palladia) is an image or other object of great antiquity on which the safety of a city or nation is said to depend. The word is a generalization from the name of the original Trojan Palladium, a wooden statue (xoanon) of Pallas Athena that Odysseus and Diomedes stole from the citadel of Troy.

items.name: the Wooden Horse
items.description: Bronze Wooden Horse statue among the Acropolis offerings, recalling the Trojan stratagem.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Trojan Horse was a wooden horse said to have been used by the Greeks during the Trojan War to sneak into the city of Troy and win the war. The Trojan Horse is not mentioned in Homer's Iliad, with the poem ending before the war is concluded, and it is only briefly mentioned in the Odyssey.

items.name: the horn of Amalthea
items.description: Horn dedicated by Miltiades in the Sicyonian treasury at Olympia.

wikipedia.lead: In classical antiquity, the cornucopia, also called the horn of plenty, is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts. In Greek, it was called the horn of Amalthea (Ancient Greek: κέρας Ἀμαλθείας, romanized: kéras Amaltheías), after Amalthea, a nurse of Zeus, who is often part of stories of the horn's origin.

items.name: the shoulder-blade of Pelops
items.description: Pelops' bone, needed to take Troy, recovered from the sea and kept by the Eleans.

items.name: the Athene of the Parthenon
names: the ivory and gold statue of Athene
items.description: Ivory and gold statue of Athene in the Parthenon, with Pandora's birth on its base.

wikipedia.lead: The statue of Athena Parthenos was a monumental chryselephantine sculpture of the goddess Athena. Attributed to Phidias and dated to the mid-fifth century BCE, it was an offering from the city of Athens to Athena, its tutelary deity.

items.name: the chest of Cypselus
items.description: Cedar chest carved with myth scenes and inscriptions, kept in Hera's temple at Olympia; once hid the infant Cypselus.

items.name: the throne of Amyclaean Apollo
items.description: Throne carved with many mythological scenes, made by Bathycles around the Amyclae statue of Apollo.
